acceptance_criteria: Discover PHP 5.x, 7.x, and 8.x side-by-side runtime instances using bounded path/process discovery with strict path validation and no shell interpolation; report discovery gaps and truncation.

Keep package-installed runtimes, executable files, CLI runtime probes, and active FPM/Apache workers as distinct subjects with stable unique identities and exact source provenance; never reduce them to one host PHP version.

Bind every runtime-specific configuration, SAPI, package provenance, worker executable identity, advisory applicability, and patch verdict to its exact runtime subject; ambiguity or cross-version conflicts remain unknown.

Add offline fixtures and positive/negative tests for PHP 5.6, 7.4, 8.2, two or more installed versions, multiple active workers, missing or deleted executables, conflicting package/runtime versions, path traversal and discovery limits.
Preserve existing PHP 8.2–8.5 behavior and evidence semantics; clarify in documentation that PHP 8.2+ is the audit-tool runtime requirement while target hosts may contain PHP 5.x/7.x.

Update the roadmap to record PRA-4-MAINLINE complete with its existing PHP 8.5 container-smoke limitation and keep Local MVP gated on PRA-5 remediation-plan completion; no claim that the Local MVP is complete.
Run all required Contract validation on the exact candidate, obtain distinct fresh correctness and blind-spot reviews, and bind deterministic verification to that same candidate.
goal: Extend the local PHP inventory and assessment to identify legacy PHP 5.x and 7.x installations and multiple concurrent PHP runtime instances without conflating installed binaries/packages, CLI runtimes, web workers, or configuration. Keep each applicability and patch result bound to exact runtime evidence.
non_goals: Do not change the collector execution requirement of PHP 8.2 or claim PHP 5.x/7.x are supported to run the audit tool.
Do not infer vulnerability, exploitability, compromise, or vendor support status from an old upstream version alone; vendor backports and unknown evidence remain individually sourced and scoped.
No source-code taint analysis, incident forensics, remediation application, network scanning, host mutation, public service, or PRA-3A.
